text:
[NTST.3.1] The mock clock moves only when the test moves it, and there are
two ways to move it: set it to an absolute instant, or advance it by a
duration. Both act on the monotonic clock ([LTIM.2.8.2]); an advance also moves
the wall clock by the same duration, and leaves a wall clock that has no value
without one. A third, `ds_engine_wall_clock_set`, sets
the wall clock alone, to any instant, earlier or later — the way a test
reproduces a host clock being stepped ([LTIM.2.8.3]).

The monotonic clock never decreases, so once the engine has taken its first
sample, from an input or a pump ([LTIM.2.8.4]), `ds_engine_clock_set` to a
value below the current one must return `DS_ERR_STATE` and leave both clocks as
they were, so nothing recorded goes backward. Before the first sample, it must
take any value, which is how a test fixes its epoch.

**An advance never wraps a clock.** On a mock clock,
`ds_engine_clock_advance` must return `DS_ERR_TIME_RANGE` and leave the engine as
it was when any of these holds:

- the duration is greater than $2^{63} - 1$, which no `Duration` holds
  ([LTIM.1.3.1]);
- the wall clock has a value, and that value plus the duration is greater than
  $2^{63} - 1$, outside the `Time` range ([LTIM.1.1.5]);
- the monotonic clock plus the duration is greater than $2^{64} - 1$, where it
  would wrap and so decrease ([LTIM.2.8.2]).

An advance that lands exactly on the top of a range is taken. A wall clock that
has no value limits nothing.

The first two exist because tests need both. An absolute set establishes an epoch,
which is what makes a computed deadline readable in the test's own text
([NTST.6.1]). A relative advance steps past a known interval without the test
having to know where the clock currently stands.

Neither is legal in live mode ([NTST.3.2]). Neither is a sample: the next
input or pump observes and records the value it left ([NTST.3.3]), and
neither on its own retracts anything, because time-driven work happens at the
next pump ([NTST.3.4]).

idris.name: Ntst_3_1__mock
idris.note: The mock engine's clocks, and whether an input has been consumed -- the state the refusal is decided on.

idris.name: Ntst_3_1__mutation
idris.note: The three mutations the clause names: a set of the monotonic clock to an instant (`ds_engine_clock_set`), an advance of both clocks by a duration (`ds_engine_clock_advance`), a set of the wall clock alone (`ds_engine_wall_clock_set`).

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__mock_replay_at_samples
idris.note: A mock run of the clause's three mutations and inputs, recorded at samples, replays from any starting clocks to the samples it held.

idris.name: ntst_3_1__advance_moves_both_alike
idris.note: AN ADVANCE MOVES BOTH CLOCKS ALIKE: across it each clock has moved by the duration, whatever the clocks were and whether or not an input has been consumed. 'An advance also moves the wall clock by the same duration.'

idris.name: ntst_3_1__after_it
idris.note: AFTER IT the same set is refused and the clocks are as they were. Computed.

idris.name: ntst_3_1__before_the_first_input
idris.note: BEFORE THE FIRST INPUT a set below the current value is taken: a test fixes its epoch. Computed.

idris.name: ntst_3_1__mono_never_decreases
idris.note: THE MONOTONIC CLOCK NEVER DECREASES across one mutation once an input has been consumed, for every mutation and every pair of clocks: the refusal of a set below the current value is how [LTIM.2.8.2]'s first sentence is kept on the mock.

idris.name: ntst_3_1__mutate
idris.note: ONE MUTATION: a set before the first input takes any value ('how a test fixes its epoch'); after it `set_at` decides; an advance moves both clocks by the duration; a wall set moves the wall clock alone, to any instant.

idris.name: ntst_3_1__mutate_shape
idris.note: No mutation un-consumes.

idris.name: ntst_3_1__run
idris.note: A run of mutations, in order.

idris.name: ntst_3_1__run_never_decreases
idris.note: AND ACROSS ANY RUN: for every sequence of mutations from a state that has consumed an input, the monotonic clock ends at or above where it began.

idris.name: ntst_3_1__set_at
idris.note: A set once an input has been consumed, decided on the comparison: taken when the value is at or above the monotonic clock, refused below it. The clause's `DS_ERR_STATE` is the refusal; the error value itself is not modelled, only that the clocks stand.

idris.name: ntst_3_1__set_at_lte
idris.note: A decided set never puts the monotonic clock below where it was.

idris.name: ntst_3_1__set_at_shape
idris.note: No decided set un-consumes: the state after it is some pair of clocks with `consumed` still set.

idris.name: ntst_3_1__unguarded
idris.note: An engine that takes every set, consumed or not. The refused shape.

idris.name: ntst_3_1__unguarded_goes_back
idris.note: WITHOUT THE REFUSAL THE MONOTONIC CLOCK GOES BACK: set to 3 at 5 after an input, it reads below 5. What the refusal is for, by the engine that lacks it.

idris.name: Ltim_2_8_3__step
idris.note: A FIXTURE'S STEP WITH THE WALL: a wall step, or one of Rete/NetworkTimed.idr's -- a tick, a data input, a pump. The clause's three mutations are a tick (a set of the monotonic clock), a tick then a wall step (an advance of both) and a wall step (a set of the wall alone). LESS than the clause: the refusal of a monotonic set below the current value is MockClock.idr's.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__wall_step_moves_no_monotonic_pump
idris.note: A wall set between two pumps changes nothing a `dwell` or `within` rule computes at the second: 'neither on its own retracts anything', and this one fires nothing either.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__no_wall_step_is_the_timed_run
idris.note: WITH NO WALL STEP THE RUN IS Rete/NetworkTimed.idr's: step for step, verdict for verdict, over every program, step list and state. By induction on the steps. Every fixture whose lowering writes no wall step -- every fixture with no `now()` -- runs the run it ran before this rung.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__run_steps_wall
idris.note: The mutations and the inputs in the fixture's order, each inside one call. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_set_projects
idris.note: 'Sets the wall clock alone': nothing of the monotonic clock, the deadlines or the facts moves. A transcription.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_set_sets_the_wall
idris.note: 'To any instant, earlier or later': the instant named is the one held. A transcription.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_set_timed
idris.note: `ds_engine_wall_clock_set` on the Idris model's engine, 'sets the wall clock alone, to any instant, earlier or later'; and the wall half of an advance, which the fixture lowering writes as a tick then a wall step. LESS than the clause: the refusal of a monotonic set below the current value is MockClock.idr's, and the lowering refuses such a fixture before anything is lowered.

idris.name: ntst_3_1__advance
idris.note: AN ADVANCE to `t`, from clocks that started together: a tick to `t` then a wall step to `t`. 'An advance also moves the wall clock by the same duration.' A fixture.

idris.name: ntst_3_1__assert_ping
idris.note: The assert of the Ping, named. A fixture.

idris.name: ntst_3_1__pump
idris.note: A pump of fuel 3, named. A fixture.
